what_disagrees: Which source Grassmann's translation is dependent on. DEP-021 gives source_a SRC-074 (Grassmann 1876-7 translation) and source_b SRC-026. SRC-026 is E. V. Arnold, Vedic Metre in its Historical Development, Cambridge 1905 - a monograph on metre with no bearing on translator independence. DEP-021's own relationship prose describes something else entirely: 'Grassmann 1876-7 translation and Grassmann Woerterbuch zum Rig-Veda are the same author, working the same decade on the same text.' The Woerterbuch is not a separate ledger row in this repository at all: its glosses reach the registers through info/matched_lemmata.json inside the SRC-069 / SRC-019 clone.
measured: One pointer, wrong. The prose, the effect_on_status and the use the registers make of DEP-021 are all correct and consistent; only source_b resolves to the wrong source.
severity: MEDIUM - low as an error, medium as a trap. Anyone following source_b to check the dependency lands on Arnold's metre monograph, finds nothing about translators, and may conclude the dependency is unfounded. PUR4J-022 rests on DEP-021 for the statement that the translators are not independent witnesses, and 06-BRIEFS/childrens-pilot/04-rules-and-gates.md gate G-06 rests on it in turn.
resolvable_here: NO - not without deciding what the correct source_b is. Grassmann's Woerterbuch has no ledger row, so the fix is either to allocate one for the glosses as carried in matched_lemmata.json, or to point source_b at SRC-069 / SRC-019 with the file named. That is a ledger decision and this unit performed no retrieval and wrote no ledger row.
effect: The independence caps DEP-021 imposes are unaffected and remain correct. What is affected is checkability: the row cannot be verified by following its own pointer.
